content: Whether or not the beloved is actually present, whether or not he is still alive at all, ceases somehow to be of importance.
author: Viktor Frankl
sourceWork: Yes to Life: In Spite of Everything (1946)
story:
Rather than offering a polite platitude, this observation challenges how we navigate our inner lives. Reminding yourself of your mortality is not morbid; it is the most clarifying lens available to human consciousness. When you remember that your days are strictly numbered, petty resentments and trivial anxieties evaporate.

Across his life and work, Viktor Frankl saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Death gives urgency and sweetness to every ordinary afternoon. Because this day will never come again, the way you spend your attention right now is of monumental significance.
reflectionPrompt: How can acknowledging your vulnerability help you build deeper self-trust and inner peace?
